## Triage — `bug` · `domain:ui` · `priority:p2` · `pm:queue`

Graded by the `domain:ui` seat (session `session_012wwHa4aaFybxXrfmfHioDM`). Queued behind three running lanes; dispatched when one frees.

### Pre-ruling, so the dispatch is short when it goes out

The card offers A / B / C as a maintainer's call. Two of the three do not actually need one:

- **B is a defect repair, not a design choice, and it is the dispatchable half.** `showStartEndColumns` returns `taskListWidth >= 280`, and its own comment says the threshold exists so that *"below this threshold the title would collapse to a few pixels."* At the 320px default the gate admits columns costing 160px and leaves the title 53px. **The function produces the exact outcome its comment names as the thing it prevents.** That is a self-refuting gate, and fixing it needs no product decision — the intent is written directly above the code.
- **C is contract-widening** (a new key on `GanttConfigSchema`, which the card confirms declares 19 keys and no width). That routes through `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`, whose quota is currently **exhausted**. Not dispatchable today regardless of its merits.
- **A** — sizing the default from the container — is the genuine design call, since it changes layout for every gantt at every viewport. Left for the maintainer.

So B ships alone, which the card's own closing sentence already permits: *"A and B are independent and both cheap; either alone lifts the title above the 'few pixels'."*

### ⚠️ The one thing the lane must verify before B is safe

Raising the threshold means the Start/End columns **disappear** at the 320px default. That is only non-destructive if the dates remain on screen elsewhere. The card asserts they do — *"each row renders `8/26 → 9/2` as a sublabel directly under the title"* — and that single sentence is the whole safety argument for B.

It will be dispatched as an assumption to falsify, not as a finding. If the sublabel is conditional (on row height, a compact mode, a config key, or a missing end date), then B removes information rather than de-duplicating it, and the shape has to change. A measurement, not a reading, decides that.

### Why the report is strong

The splitter drag is a genuine control, not an illustration: same data, same page, same build, panel 320 to 580, title client width 53 to 260, needed 260 throughout. That isolates width as the entire cause and rules out font, overflow rules, and the data itself in one move.

Also correctly identified: the `gantt` block is a passthrough object, so an invented `gantt.taskListWidth` would pass author-time validation and be **silently ignored** — which is why this was filed rather than worked around. That is the same silent-inert class as #7199.

## Claimed and dispatched — `domain:ui` execution seat

- **session** `session_012wwHa4aaFybxXrfmfHioDM`
- **branch** `claude/issue-7204-gantt-tasklist-width`

All agents share one GitHub identity, so the assignee field alone does not identify whose claim this is. If your session ID differs from the one above, this card is taken.

Dispatched as **option B only**, per the ruling already recorded in the triage comment above: the Start/End threshold is a defect repair, not a design choice, because `showStartEndColumns` produces the exact outcome its own comment names as the thing it prevents. Option A (sizing from the container) stays the maintainer's call; option C is contract-widening and tier-blocked regardless.

### The one thing the lane is told to falsify before shipping

B's entire safety argument is a single sentence in the report — that each row already renders `8/26 → 9/2` as a sublabel under the title, so removing the two date columns de-duplicates rather than deletes. That sentence is dispatched as an **assumption to falsify, not a finding**, with an explicit instruction to stop and report if the sublabel turns out to be conditional on row height, a compact mode, a config key, or a missing end date.

This is not boilerplate caution. Twice this shift a lane has come back having falsified one of my premises — #7179's "single `$select` build site" (there are two, and a one-site fix would have shipped green and broken) and #7199's "`description` is the only unrelayed key" (there are three). Both were caught only because the order required verifying the PM's readings, not just the card's. This card's premise is one unverified sentence carrying the whole change, so it gets the same treatment.

## ⛔ Option B CANNOT ship as I ruled it — my ruling was wrong, and the lane proved it

`domain:ui` seat, session `session_012wwHa4aaFybxXrfmfHioDM`. No code shipped, no PR, and that is the correct outcome. Clearing `pm:dispatched`; re-grading to `needs-user-decision`.

### What I ruled, and why it was wrong

I ruled option B a **defect repair, not a design choice** — on the argument that `showStartEndColumns` produces the outcome its own comment names as the thing it prevents. That reading of the gate still stands.

What does not stand is the safety argument I built on top of it. B is only non-destructive if removing the two date columns *de-duplicates* the dates rather than deleting them, and the card's one sentence for that was:

> each row renders `8/26 → 9/2` as a sublabel directly under the title

**That sentence is conditional, and it is false at exactly the widths where this defect lives.** The sublabel span carries `gantt-sm-hidden`, and `GanttView` injects its own style element containing `@media (min-width: 640px) { .gantt-sm-hidden { display: none; } }`.

Measured in a real Chromium against the component's own emitted markup and its own injected style element:

| viewport | sublabel `display` | client width |
|---:|---|---:|
| 500 | `inline` | 72.9px |
| 639 | `inline` | 72.9px |
| **640** | **`none`** | **0** |
| 800 / 1024 / 1440 / 1920 | `none` | 0 |

So at every desktop width — including the 1440 and 1920 where the truncation was reported — the sublabel is already `display: none`. **Raising the threshold as I ruled would delete a row's dates, not de-duplicate them.** It would have traded a truncated name for a missing date and shipped looking like a fix.

This is the third PM premise a lane has falsified this shift, and the first where the falsified premise was load-bearing for a **ruling** rather than a mechanism note. The order said a clean stop on a falsified premise is a full success. It is, and this is what one looks like.

### The measurement discipline is why this was caught rather than confirmed

⭐ **jsdom would have given a false confirmation, in the reassuring direction.** `getComputedStyle(sublabel).display` returned `none` at 500, 800 **and** 1440 alike, because jsdom applies the media rule irrespective of `innerWidth`. Reported as **NOT MEASURED** rather than as a result, and the decisive reading moved to a real browser. Had that been taken at face value, the conclusion would have been "the sublabel is never visible" — different from the truth, and it would have sent the fix somewhere else entirely.

Two more things done right:

- **No ablation was invented.** With nothing implemented there was nothing to ablate, and the report says so — *"an ablation with nothing to ablate would be theatre"* — rather than manufacturing a colour to fill the field.
- **The title width was derived from source, not copied from the card.** 320 − 32 padding − 80 Start − 80 End − 28 open slot = 100px name cell; minus 32px of furniture = 68px, or 54px at depth 1. That lands within 1px of the card's measured 53 — an independent derivation agreeing with the report, which is worth more than adopting its table.

### A live defect found on the way: #7224

At any viewport between **640 and 1023**, the default task-list width is 220, so `showStartEndColumns(220)` is false and the columns are off — while the sublabel is *already* `display: none` from 640 up. **A row shows no dates at all.** That is on current `main`, today, and it also holds at 1024+ whenever a persisted drag left the panel under 280.

The root is that **two gates read two different widths** — a ResizeObserver container measurement and a CSS viewport media query — and neither is the complement of the other. That is the actual defect behind this card, and it is a better description of the problem than the one the card (or I) had.

### Escalated, not decided

The shape question goes to the maintainer with a recommendation rather than being ruled from this seat, because the leading option changes how every gantt row looks:

**Recommended: option A** — render the sublabel exactly when the Start/End columns are *not* painted, then raise the threshold. One predicate instead of two that can drift apart; it also closes #7224 at its root. Cost, stated plainly: every desktop row gains a second line. That is a look-and-feel change across every gantt, which is why it needs a yes rather than my say-so.

⛔ **Option C — ship B and let the dates leave the task list — is now clearly wrong**, and the lane found the reason: the hover-tooltip fallback prints dates **only when `task.fields` is empty**, so the documented `tooltipFields` key removes that fallback too. It would also silently remove inline date **editing**, since the two `type="date"` inputs live in those very cells.

On the threshold, if one is still needed: the derived floor is **412** (32 padding + 160 columns + 28 open slot + 32 furniture + 160 reusing `TASK_LIST_MIN_W`), not the card's suggested 440, which is not derived from anything. ⚠️ But note what 412 implies: the columns would be off at **all three defaults** (140 / 220 / 320), so the threshold would only ever be cleared by a manual drag — *a removal of the feature by arithmetic*, which is not what the ruling asked for. That is another reason the shape has to be settled before any number is.

Carried to #5560.

## Maintainer ruling recorded — Y: one container-driven predicate, and the task-list default sized from the container (ruled together with #7224)

Director seat (objectstack #12708), summon #8, session `session_01ShyhexkB2d1AeRZ85tgAAe`, 2026-09-02.

Provenance (who / verbatim / where): maintainer, live PM chat with the director seat, 2026-09-02, replying to decision batch #5 in which this card and #7224 were items 2 and 3, presented as one ruling with the recommendation Y (fallback X). Verbatim reply: 「同意」.

**Ruled: Y.** Three parts, one PR:

1. **One predicate, container-driven.** The date sublabel renders exactly when the Start/End columns are not painted, and both read the same container width — the viewport media rule on `gantt-sm-hidden` goes; "the columns are painted" stops being the conjunction of a container test and a viewport test. This closes #7224's 640–1023 band (and the dragged-narrow case at any width) at the root.
2. **The task-list default is sized from the container**, a clamped share rather than the 320px cap: at 1440 and wider the panel takes enough of the extra width that a 25–40 character title is legible while the Start/End columns stay on; the exact share and clamp bounds are the dev's to derive and pin at 1280 / 1440 / 1920, with 320 as the floor.
3. **The Start/End threshold is the derived 412** (32 padding + 160 columns + 28 open-details slot + 32 title furniture + 160 minimum title, each term traced to source), not the estimated 440. With part 2 in place the desktop defaults clear it; below it the sublabel carries the dates, so inline date editing stays reachable at desktop defaults.

Option X (predicate + threshold only) is the recorded fallback; option C (an authorable width key) is not taken — no new key. The gantt-block passthrough (an invented `gantt.taskListWidth` validates and is ignored) is noted as the same silent-inert class as #7199 and is not repaired here.

Execution: `domain:ui` lane, one dispatch for both cards (same file, same two functions), branch may continue from the empty probe `claude/issue-7204-gantt-tasklist-width`. Layout only, no contract change ⇒ Clause-② no. Tests: the #7224 viewport table in a real browser (sublabel visible iff columns hidden, at 500 / 639 / 640 / 800 / 1024 / 1440 / 1920), and the title client width at the three desktop widths above the legibility floor.

State transition, same stroke: `needs-user-decision` → `pm:queue`; `bug`, `priority:p2` retained. Ledger: objectstack director seat post #12708, summon #8.

Measured against PR #7391's branch: it touches **6 files** under `packages/plugin-gantt/`, and `GanttView.tsx` is **not** among them — zero hits, with a firing control (33 changed files total). The dispatch requires the measurement.

### What the previous round bought, and why this dispatch is short

This card was dispatched once before and came back with **no code and a falsified premise** — correctly. Option B's entire safety argument was one sentence ("each row renders the dates as a sublabel"), and it is **false at every desktop width**: the sublabel carries `gantt-sm-hidden`, and `GanttView` injects `@media (min-width: 640px) { .gantt-sm-hidden { display: none } }`. Raising the threshold as first ruled would have **deleted** a row's dates while looking like a fix.

⭐ That round also produced the trap this one must not fall into: **jsdom gives a false confirmation here, in the reassuring direction** — it applies the media rule irrespective of `innerWidth`, returning `display: none` at 500, 800 and 1440 alike. The decisive reading has to come from a real browser. It is carried into the dispatch as a named hazard.

And it produced #7224 as a live defect on `main`: between 640 and 1023 the columns are gated off by a container test while the sublabel is gated off by a viewport test, so **a row shows no dates at all**. Two gates reading two different widths, neither the complement of the other — that is the actual root, and it is why the two cards ship together.
